_meta.source: docs/research/cover-letter/00-playbook.md §5 and rules CL-70 to CL-78 (audit 2026-10-18, 09 #8). Shape only: never a source of facts. Each note applies only when the student's own answers or CV give the material for it.

finance_banking: Investment banking: structure it as why the firm, why the division, why you. Name the division and office from the job post.

Markets: name the desk family the job post names (rates, FX, credit, equities, structuring) and show engagement with markets from the student's own answers or CV (a competition, a portfolio, a market view). 'Interest in markets' alone fails.
Asset management: a buy-side reason and the firm's investment style or asset class, only if the job post or picked facts state it. Don't reuse investment-banking motivation.
Audit, tax and other Big 4 roles: show you understand the qualification (ACA, CTA, ACCA) and what the service line does day to day. 'Why this firm' must not fit the other three Big 4 firms.
Actuarial: mention IFoA exam progress and the line of business only when the CV or answers give them.
Never give salary, bonus, perks, prestige or exit opportunities as the motivation.
quant_trading: Keep it factual and short; quant firms screen on academics, competitions, projects and tests.
'Additional information' boxes: at most 150 words, covering only why this firm, how the student heard of it and their timeline.
Never give salary, bonus or prestige as the motivation.
consulting: Name the office from the job post; office specificity matters.
Never frame consulting as a stepping stone ('a few years', 'exit opportunities', 'keeping my options open').
Structure the student's story as problem, what they did, result, using only what the CV and answers say.
software_eng: Proof over adjectives: describe what the student built and its effect (users, speed, rank) as the CV states it, rather than listing the tech stack.
One or two proof links the student owns (GitHub, a demo) belong in the CV, not invented here.
data_analytics: Each story runs question, method, decision; tool names come second. (Soft guidance: the evidence for this sector is weak.)
product: One observation about the firm's own product, taken only from the student's answers, plus a hypothesis. Never invent product usage; if there is no such answer, leave it out.
marketing_growth: Name the channel or campaign the student actually ran, with its result only as the CV states it.
research: Name the specific work or group from the job post and connect it to the student's own project or methods; keep it plain and specific.
